title: Maize (Zea mays)
content_en: Maize is one of the most important staple crops in Rwanda, grown across all altitude zones. Grown in 900–2000 m. Seasons: Season A (Sep-Feb), Season B (Mar-Jun). Common problems include: fall-armyworm, maize-streak-virus, gray-leaf-spot, nitrogen-deficiency, drought-stress, stalk-borer.

title: Maize prevention tips
content_en: Prevention tips for Maize: Use certified seeds from approved suppliers. Practice crop rotation with legumes. Monitor fields regularly, especially during early vegetative stages. Ensure proper spacing to reduce humidity and disease pressure. Apply fertiliser according to RAB recommendations.

Genzura inzu z'imyaka buri gihe, cyane cyane mu bihe bya mbere by'imikurire. Jya ukora umuzi w'ibigori neza kugira ngo ugabanye ubuhehere n'indwara. Shira ifumbire hakurikijwe inama za RAB.

title: Beans (Phaseolus vulgaris)
content_en: Beans are a primary protein source and cash crop for Rwandan farmers, grown in both seasons. Grown in 1000–2000 m. Seasons: Season A (Sep-Feb), Season B (Mar-Jun). Common problems include: bean-fly, angular-leaf-spot, bean-rust, pythium-root-rot, potassium-deficiency, waterlogging.
content_rw: Ibishyimbo ni inkomoko y'ibwoya kandi ni umusaruro w'amafaranga ku barima b'u Rwanda. Biragundwa mu 1000–2000 m. Ibihe: Season A (Sep-Feb), Season B (Mar-Jun).
keywords: beans | beans | ibishyimbo | phaseolus vulgaris

title: Beans prevention tips
content_en: Prevention tips for Beans: Use disease-resistant varieties recommended by RAB. Avoid planting in poorly drained soils. Practice crop rotation — do not plant beans in the same field every season. Inspect young seedlings for bean fly damage within the first two weeks. Remove and destroy infected plant material.
content_rw: Inama zo kurinda Ibishyimbo: Koresha ubwoko bw'imbuto bwuzuye indwara bushyigikiwe na RAB. Irinde gutera mu butaka butagira imiringoti myiza y'amazi. Hindura imyaka — ntukore ibishyimbo mu murima umwe buri gihembwe. Genzura inshyitsi nto ku biribwa by'ibibondo mu cyumweru cya mbere n'icya kabiri. Vana kandi ukumbye ibimera byanduye.
keywords: beans | prevention | tips

title: Cassava (Manihot esculenta)
content_en: Cassava is a drought-tolerant food security crop grown widely in lower-altitude Rwanda. Grown in 700–1800 m. Seasons: Year-round with seasonal planting. Common problems include: cassava-mosaic-disease, cassava-brown-streak, cassava-mealybug, whitefly, zinc-deficiency, waterlogging.
content_rw: Imyumbati ni umusaruro w'umutekano w'ibiribwa ushobora guhangana n'amapfa, uragundwa cyane mu ntera zaba hasi mu Rwanda. Biragundwa mu 700–1800 m. Ibihe: Year-round with seasonal planting.
keywords: cassava | cassava | imyumbati | manihot esculenta

title: Cassava prevention tips
content_en: Prevention tips for Cassava: Use CMD-resistant and CBSD-tolerant varieties. Only plant certified, disease-free cuttings. Remove and destroy mosaic-infected plants immediately. Control whitefly populations which spread mosaic virus. Avoid introducing planting material from infected areas.
content_rw: Inama zo kurinda Imyumbati: Koresha ubwoko bwuzuye CMD no kugumya CBSD. Tera gusa gacaca emerewe, nta ndwara. Vana kandi ukumbye imyumbati yanduye indwara ya mosaic vuba. Genzura inyoni zo gutera amata mu buhehere zivura virusi ya mosaic. Irinde gutera gacaca iturutse mu turere twanduye.

title: Irish Potato (Solanum tuberosum)
content_en: Irish potato is a major cash and food crop grown primarily in the high-altitude regions of Rwanda. Grown in 1500–2800 m. Seasons: Season A (Sep-Feb), Season B (Mar-Jun). Common problems include: late-blight, early-blight, potato-virus-y, aphids, phosphorus-deficiency, frost-damage.
content_rw: Ibirayi ni umusaruro w'amafaranga n'ibiribwa by'ingenzi biragundwa cyane mu turere two hejuru mu Rwanda. Biragundwa mu 1500–2800 m. Ibihe: Season A (Sep-Feb), Season B (Mar-Jun).
keywords: irish-potato | irish potato | ibirayi | solanum tuberosum

title: Irish Potato prevention tips
content_en: Prevention tips for Irish Potato: Use certified, blight-resistant seed tubers. Apply copper-based fungicides preventively during rainy seasons. Earthing up reduces tuber exposure to blight spores. Avoid overhead irrigation which promotes blight spread. Inspect fields twice weekly during high blight risk periods.
content_rw: Inama zo kurinda Ibirayi: Koresha imbuto z'ibirayi emerewe, zuzuye late blight. Koresha ubuvuzi bwa fungicide ya kobre mbere y'igihe mu bihe by'imvura. Kubita ubutaka munsi y'ibirayi bigabanya kubonekera kwa blight ku cyori. Irinde gusukura amazi mu bwirukane bibasha gutera blight gukwirakwira. Genzura inzu z'imyaka inshuro ebyiri mu cyumweru mu bihe bya blight bya hejuru.
keywords: irish-potato | prevention | tips

title: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum)
content_en: Tomatoes are grown as a cash crop across Rwanda, particularly in lowland and valley areas. Grown in 900–1800 m. Seasons: Year-round under irrigation. Common problems include: early-blight, late-blight, tomato-leaf-miner, whitefly, bacterial-wilt, blossom-end-rot, magnesium-deficiency.

keywords: tomato | tomato | inyanya | solanum lycopersicum

title: Tomato prevention tips
content_en: Prevention tips for Tomato: Use grafted or resistant tomato varieties for blight-prone areas. Practice crop rotation — avoid planting in fields with recent solanaceous crops. Install yellow sticky traps to monitor and reduce whitefly populations. Avoid excessive nitrogen which promotes vegetative growth over fruiting. Ensure adequate calcium availability to prevent blossom end rot.
content_rw: Inama zo kurinda Inyanya: Koresha ubwoko bw'inyanya yashongewe cyangwa yuzuye indwara mu turere two kugirwa n'indwara ya blight. Hindura imyaka — irinde gutera mu mirima yari ifite ibimera bya solanaceous vuba aha. Shira imishono ishungura umuhondo kugira ngo urebe kandi ugabanye inyoni zo gutera amata mu buhehere. Irinde azote nyinshi zitera imikurire y'amashami aho gutera imbuto. Menya neza ko kalisiyo ihari bihagije kugira ngo wirinde kurota kw'imbuto.

title: Fall Armyworm (Pest)
content_en: Fall Armyworm affects maize. Symptoms: Irregular holes and ragged feeding on leaves Window-pane damage on young leaves Sawdust-like frass near the whorl Larvae hiding in the maize whorl during the day Complete defoliation in severe cases. Recommendations: Inspect nearby maize plants, especially the whorl, for larvae. Monitor the affected field every 2–3 days. Use fall armyworm pheromone traps for early detection. Apply locally approved biological or chemical control following RAB guidance. Contact an agronomist if the infestation spreads rapidly.
content_rw: Inzito y'ibigori ingenzi ku maize. Ibimenyetso: Imyanya idahindura n'amababi yafunguye nabi Impanuka nk'amadirishwa ku mababi mata Mu gihindure amatunguru ya sawdust hafi y'uruhinja Udukoko two mu ruhinja rw'ibigori mu manya Kw'amababi yose mu bihe bikomeye. Inama: Genzura ibigori byo hafi, cyane cyane uruhinja, urebe utudomoko. Komeza genzura umurima buri minsi 2–3. Koresha uturingo twa pheromone kugira ngo menye vuba. Koresha uburyo bwemewe na RAB bwo kurwanya utudomoko. Vuga umuhinzi w'ubuhinzi niba bibanduka vuba.
keywords: armyworm | insects | holes | leaves | whorl | frass | maize

title: Maize Stalk Borer (Pest)
content_en: Maize Stalk Borer affects maize. Symptoms: Deadheart symptoms in young plants Holes in the stem and wilting Sawdust-like frass at entry holes Stunted growth and yellowing. Recommendations: Inspect stems for bore holes and frass. Remove and destroy infested plants. Use crop rotation to disrupt the pest cycle. Follow RAB-approved integrated pest management.
content_rw: Udukoro ku biti by'ibigori ingenzi ku maize. Ibimenyetso: Imypanuka yo gufa y'imitima mu birimwa bibiri Imyanda ku giti n'ukweyize Amatunguru ya sawdust ku myanda y'injira Kugenda nabi no guhindura umuhondo. Inama: Genzura imisatsi urebe imyanda n'amatunguru. Vana kandi ukumye ibiribwa byanduye. Hindura imyaka kugira ngo ugabanye umuzunguko w'udomoko. Kurikiza inama za RAB zo kugenzura udokoko.
keywords: stalk | borer | stem | holes | wilting | maize

title: Bean Fly (Pest)
content_en: Bean Fly affects beans. Symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of seedlings Tunnels in the stem base Stunted or dead young plants Split stems reveal maggots. Recommendations: Inspect seedlings within 1–2 weeks of emergence. Use seed treatment with RAB-approved insecticide. Remove and destroy infected plants. Plant in rotation and avoid consecutive bean crops.

Ibimenyetso: Guhindura umuhondo n'ukweyize ku bibondo Imyanda mu gice cyo hasi cy'igiti Ibibondo bikomeza nabi cyangwa bi fite Mu gukomata ibiti byerekana amafi. Inama: Genzura ibibondo mu cyumweru cya 1–2 cyo kubyara. Koresha ubuvuzi bw'imbuto na RAB wemewe. Vana kandi ukumye ibimera byanduye. Tera ukoresheje guhindura imyaka, irinde gutera ibishyimba buri gihe.
keywords: bean | fly | seedling | yellow | wilting | maggot

title: Aphids (Pest)
content_en: Aphids affects irish-potato, tomato. Symptoms: Clusters of small soft-bodied insects under leaves Curled or distorted leaves Sticky honeydew on the plant surface Sooty mould growth on honeydew. Recommendations: Monitor for aphid colonies under leaves. Use insecticidal soap or neem-based sprays. Encourage natural predators like ladybirds. Remove heavily infested plant parts. Follow RAB-approved pest control guidance.

title: Whitefly (Pest)
content_en: Whitefly affects cassava, tomato. Symptoms: Small white insects flying when plant is disturbed Yellowing and curling of leaves Whitefly nymphs on the underside of leaves Virus-like symptoms on cassava (mosaic). Recommendations: Install yellow sticky traps to monitor adults. Remove weeds that host whitefly. Use RAB-approved insecticide if infestation is severe. Control whitefly to reduce virus transmission.

title: Cassava Mealybug (Pest)
content_en: Cassava Mealybug affects cassava. Symptoms: White cottony masses on stems and leaf bases Stunted and distorted plant growth Yellowing and premature leaf drop Reduced tuber yield. Recommendations: Inspect stems and leaf bases for white masses. Use biological control — parasitoid wasps where available. Remove and burn heavily infested plants. Plant clean, mealybug-free cuttings.

title: Maize Streak Virus (Disease)
content_en: Maize Streak Virus affects maize. Symptoms: Chlorotic streaks along leaf veins Yellowish parallel streaks on young leaves Stunted and severely reduced yield Spread by leafhoppers. Recommendations: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Control leafhopper populations. Use MSV-resistant maize varieties. Avoid planting near infected fields.

content_en: Gray Leaf Spot affects maize. Symptoms: Gray to tan rectangular lesions on leaves Lesions parallel to leaf veins Premature leaf death in severe cases Most severe in humid conditions. Recommendations: Use resistant maize hybrids. Practice crop rotation with non-host crops. Improve field drainage and reduce humidity. Apply fungicide if severe, per RAB guidance.

content_en: Angular Leaf Spot affects beans. Symptoms: Angular brown spots on leaves Spots limited by leaf veins Yellow halo around lesions Premature defoliation. title: Late Blight (Disease)
content_en: Late Blight affects irish-potato, tomato. Symptoms: Water-soaked dark green to brown lesions on leaves White mould on underside of lesions in humid conditions Rapid leaf collapse and necrosis Tuber rot in potato. Recommendations: Use certified, blight-resistant seed. Apply copper-based fungicide preventively during rainy season. Destroy infected plants immediately. Avoid overhead irrigation. Escalate to agronomist — late blight can destroy a crop in days.
content_rw: Indwara ya late blight ingenzi ku irish-potato, tomato. Ibimenyetso: Imypanuka ya kijyagana nk'amazi ku mababi Ubukara buera munsi y'imypanuka mu bihe by'ubuhehere Kw'amababi byihuse n'ukw'ibimenyetso Gukwandura kw'ibirayi mu mafunguro. Vuga umuhinzi — late blight ishobora kwangiza umusaruro mu minsi.

title: Early Blight (Disease)
content_en: Early Blight affects irish-potato, tomato. Symptoms: Concentric ring lesions (target-spot) on leaves Yellowing around older lesions Lesions on stems and tubers Premature defoliation. Recommendations: Use resistant varieties where available. Practice crop rotation — 2–3 years without solanaceous crops. Remove infected plant debris. Apply RAB-approved fungicide.

Ibimenyetso: Imypanuka y'imirongo iburyo (target-spot) ku mababi Guhindura umuhondo hafi y'imypanuka ya kera Imypanuka ku misatsi n'ibirayi Kw'amababi vuba. title: Cassava Mosaic Disease (Disease)
content_en: Cassava Mosaic Disease affects cassava. Symptoms: Mottled, yellow and green mosaic pattern on leaves Distorted and twisted leaves Stunted plant growth Reduced tuber yield. Recommendations: Use CMD-resistant varieties (e.g. from RAB). Remove and destroy infected plants. Control whitefly which spreads the virus. Plant only disease-free cuttings.

title: Bacterial Wilt (Disease)
content_en: Bacterial Wilt affects tomato. Symptoms: Sudden wilting of the entire plant Bacterial ooze from cut stems Yellowing of lower leaves Plant death within days. Recommendations: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Avoid planting solanaceous crops in the same soil for 3+ years. Use disease-free seedlings. Escalate to agronomist — bacterial wilt is soil-borne and persistent.

Ibimenyetso: Kweyize byihuse by'ikimera cyose Ibyatsi by'ubaktiriya ku misatsi yacitwe Guhindura umuhondo kw'amababi ya hasi Gufa kw'ikimera mu minsi. Inama: Vana kandi ukumye ibimera byanduye vuba. Irinde gutera solanaceous mu butaka bumwe imyaka 3+. Koresha ibibondo nta ndwara. Vuga umuhinzi — bacterial wilt iri mu butaka kandi ikomeza.

title: Nitrogen Deficiency (NutrientDeficiency)
content_en: Nitrogen Deficiency affects maize, beans, cassava, irish-potato, tomato. Symptoms: Yellowing (chlorosis) starting from older lower leaves Stunted plant growth Pale green overall appearance Reduced tillering in cereals. Recommendations: Apply nitrogen fertiliser (urea or NPK) per RAB recommendations. Incorporate organic matter or compost. Practice crop rotation with nitrogen-fixing legumes. Test soil before fertiliser application.
content_rw: Kubura kw'azote ingenzi ku maize, beans, cassava, irish-potato, tomato. Ibimenyetso: Guhindura umuhondo (chlorosis) guturutse ku mababi ya hasi Kugenda nabi kw'ikimera Gufata mu maso y'icyatsi gikaze Kugabanya imyaka y'ibyatsi. Inama: Koresha ifumbire ya azote (urea cyangwa NPK) hakurikijwe RAB. Shyira mu butaka ibyatsi cyangwa ifumbire y'ibimera. Hindura imyaka n'ibibyimba bifasha gukora azote. Gerageza ubutaka mbere yo koresha ifumbire.

title: Potassium Deficiency (NutrientDeficiency)
content_en: Potassium Deficiency affects beans, maize, irish-potato, tomato. Symptoms: Yellowing and browning at leaf margins (edges) Symptoms on older leaves first Weak stems and lodging in cereals Poor fruit/tuber quality. Recommendations: Apply potash (KCl or NPK with K) per RAB guidance. Use compost or green manure. Test soil for potassium levels. Avoid excessive nitrogen which worsens K imbalance.

Ibimenyetso: Guhindura umuhondo n'umukara ku ngingo z'amababi Ibimenyetso ku mababi ya kera Imisatsi yereranye n'isigamira Gutanga nabi kw'imbuto cyangwa imyumbati. Inama: Koresha potashi (KCl cyangwa NPK na K) hakurikijwe RAB. Koresha ifumbire y'ibimera cyangwa compost. Gerageza ubutaka uburebure bwa potasiyumu. Irinde azote nyinshi zitera K kunanirana.

title: Phosphorus Deficiency (NutrientDeficiency)
content_en: Phosphorus Deficiency affects maize, irish-potato, beans. Symptoms: Dark green or purplish leaves Stunted root and shoot growth Delayed maturity Poor tillering. Recommendations: Apply DAP or NPK fertiliser at planting. Apply near the root zone for uptake. Use rock phosphate or organic compost on acidic soils. Test soil pH — phosphorus uptake is poor in very acidic soil.

Shyira hafi y'imizzi kugira ngo ifungure. Koresha phosphate ya butaka cyangwa compost ku butaka bworoshye. Gerageza pH y'ubutaka — phosphorus ifungura nabi mu butaka bworoshye cyane.

title: Magnesium Deficiency (NutrientDeficiency)
content_en: Magnesium Deficiency affects tomato, irish-potato. Symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis (yellow between veins) on older leaves Leaves may develop reddish or purple tint Symptoms progress upward as deficiency worsens. Recommendations: Apply magnesium sulphate (Epsom salts) or dolomitic lime. Maintain balanced soil pH. Use foliar Mg spray for quick correction. Test soil for Mg levels.

content_en: Zinc Deficiency affects cassava, maize. Recommendations: Apply zinc sulphate as soil or foliar application. Avoid over-liming which reduces zinc availability. Use zinc-enriched compound fertilisers. Test soil pH and zinc levels.

content_en: Drought Stress affects maize, beans, cassava, irish-potato, tomato. Symptoms: Wilting during the day, partial recovery at night Leaf rolling and curling Dry, brittle leaf edges Premature senescence of lower leaves. Recommendations: Apply irrigation if available, especially during critical growth stages. Use mulch to conserve soil moisture. Plant drought-tolerant varieties. Practice water harvesting and conservation tillage.

title: Waterlogging (EnvironmentalStress)
content_en: Waterlogging affects beans, cassava, tomato. Symptoms: Yellowing and wilting despite wet soil Stunted root growth and root rot Leaf drop and reduced vigour Algae or moss on the soil surface. Recommendations: Improve field drainage with raised beds or channels. Avoid planting in low-lying waterlogged areas. Use waterlogging-tolerant varieties. Reduce irrigation frequency.

title: Frost Damage (EnvironmentalStress)
content_en: Frost Damage affects irish-potato, tomato, beans. Symptoms: Water-soaked patches on leaves that turn black Wilting and blackening of young tissue Leaf curling downward Symptoms worst after cold nights. Recommendations: Avoid planting frost-sensitive crops in frost-prone valleys. Use mulch or row covers on cold nights. Plant after the last expected frost date. Irrigate lightly before frost — wet soil retains heat.
